definitions.explanation: A Japanese national holiday on the second Monday of October, to enjoy sports and promote health. It was called {体育|たいいく}の{日|ひ} until 2019.

examples.japanese: スポーツの{日|ひ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{十月|じゅうがつ}→十月：00634_juugatsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{祝日|しゅくじつ}→祝日：07588_shukujitsu⟧だ。
examples.english: Sports Day is a national holiday in October.

examples.japanese: スポーツの{日|ひ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{家族|かぞく}→家族：00552_kazoku⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦マラソン→マラソン：04732_marason⟧⟦{大会|たいかい}→大会：03386_taikai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{出|で}た→出る：00513_deru⟧。
examples.english: On Sports Day, my family ran in a marathon event.

examples.japanese: スポーツの{日|ひ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、もともと⟦{東京|とうきょう}→東京：09564_toukyou⟧⟦オリンピック→オリンピック：09899_orinpikku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{開会式|かいかいしき}→開会式：27306_kaikaishiki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{記念|きねん}→記念：00232_kinen⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{日|ひ}→日：02249_hi⟧だった。
examples.english: Sports Day originally commemorated the opening ceremony of the Tokyo Olympics.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
The holiday began in 1966 as ⟦{体育|たいいく}→体育：03384_taiiku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{日|ひ}→日：02249_hi⟧ on October 10, the day the 1964 Tokyo Olympics opened. It moved to the second Monday of October in 2000, giving a three-day weekend, and was renamed スポーツの{日|ひ} in 2020. Many schools and towns hold sports days (⟦{運動会|うんどうかい}→運動会：03013_undoukai⟧) around this time.
